source.title: Exploring Vision Transformers on the Frontier Supercomputer for Remote Sensing and Geoscientific Applications
source.authors: Valentine Anantharaj; Takuya Kurihana; Sajal Dash; Gabriele Padovani; S. Fiore

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; minor PDF/OCR layout artifacts do not prevent reading.
record.tranche_reason: Benchmarks vision-transformer test loss on remote-sensing imagery, extending scaling-related measurements to a non-text modality. It does not reproduce or fit the original language-model scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-loss comparisons across model architectures, parameter sizes and GPU counts. It does not fit power laws, test extrapolation, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The test-loss-by-energy heatmaps are composite metrics and are not recorded as loss-only results. Loss values in the plots are not numerically stated in the text.
record.test_reason: This is a preliminary HPC benchmark of two ViT backbones (MAE, SwinT-V2) on MODIS cloud tiles, focused on energy and time to solution. It fits no power law and runs only three model sizes (100M, 600M, 1B) for at most one epoch. The text never states how loss changes with model size. The node-count effect comes from a fixed one-epoch budget split across replicas, so it changes steps and global batch, not total data seen. The MAE vs SwinT-V2 comparison is between architecture families, likely with different objectives, not a depth/width shape change at fixed parameters. No row's own results bear on any version. The paper cites Hoffmann et al. and says LLM scaling lessons may transfer to ViTs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present a preliminary benchmark for picking cost-effective ViT configurations on EO data. The most energy-efficient configuration (loss × energy) is MAE 100M on one node. Fewer GPUs are generally more energy efficient, while more GPUs cut time to solution. They attribute higher loss at more nodes to DDP data sharding.
record.recipe_differences: Benchmarks MAE and SwinT-V2 on remote-sensing imagery; it does not fit or reproduce the language-model scaling-law method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported test loss changes with architecture, parameter size, and GPU/node count; the authors attribute the node-count association to data sharding in distributed data-parallel training.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed one-epoch budget with DDP, test loss rises with GPU/node count (8 to 128 GPUs) for both architectures at all sizes (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed data budget, more data-parallel replicas (fewer steps, larger global batch) raise pretraining loss for ViTs.

fits_no_version.finding: MAE has lower test loss than SwinT-V2 at 100M, but SwinT-V2 is lower at 600M (Fig. 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The ranking between ViT architecture families on remote-sensing pretraining loss flips with model size.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
record.problems: The benchmark is limited to one epoch or less and a randomly selected subset of 2 million samples. No power-law fits or numeric loss tables are provided; plotted values are not stated in the text. Some large configurations ran out of memory, and the results do not include downstream-task evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: The test-loss-by-energy heatmaps in Figure 2 are omitted because they report a loss-energy product rather than test loss alone. No separate numeric results are stated for those plots.

untested.parts: Whether ViT test loss on remote-sensing data follows a power law in parameters, data or compute. Only three sizes are run, no fit is made, and the text states no size trend.
Depth/width variation at fixed parameter count is not studied.
No language-model pretraining loss scaling is measured.
No extrapolation from small runs is made.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices are reported.

missing.what: Test loss across model sizes 100M/600M/1B within each architecture, the only material on loss versus parameters. The trend is figure-only and not stated in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4/V5 links and limits_scope labels are removed. The architecture comparison is not a shape test, and the node-count effect is a steps/batch artifact of a fixed one-epoch budget, not a scaling-law form. The authors' sharding explanation is questionable under standard DDP gradient averaging.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens or compute is not tested.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger-run losses.
No fixed-compute loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation or fitted growth trends.
Compares MAE and SwinT-V2 at 100M and 600M parameters, but does not separately vary or report depth, width, or other architecture details, and does not quantify whether loss differences are slight.

Tests vision-transformer models on remote-sensing data, but does not fit or establish a power-law form. Only a short training run of 6727 steps or less (corresponding to an epoch) is considered; repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or comparison of fitting choices is reported.
